re-rooting the tree structure also need to map evolutionary statistics to the new tree structure and some of the statistics make not make evolutionary sense after re-rooting.

Be careful if you want to this.

messages.body_plain:
I have a set of 4 trees that I would like to plot with ggtree and facet_wrap. The branches should be coloured using a continuous character that is stored in 4 different dataframes. I thought that by combining the 4 different dataframes into a single one and by replacing the tree ".id" I would be able to get similar to https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/ggtree/inst/doc/treeVisualization.html , but with branches coded according to my continuous character.
Unfortunately, this does not really work out. If I just use my combined dataframe, only some branches will be colored (see attached figure: "Plot_without_hack_missing_branches.pdf"). This is not surprising, as the associated data is assigned to the wrong trees (see ".id" column). If I try to replace the ".id" values with the correct ones and then try to plot the 4 trees, R starts calculating but never finishes (i. e., I have to stop the calculation without getting the plot).
What am I doing wrong? The replacement of the ".id" values is obviously an ugly hack - is there a better way to do this?

Reproducible example code (files "mytrees.txt" and "mydf.list.txt" are attached):

# #Example code
library(ape)
library(ggtree)

mytrees <- dget("mytrees.txt")
mydf.list <- dget("mydf.list.txt")

for(i in 1:length(mytrees)){
  mydf.list[[i]]["myTreeID"] <- as.factor(paste("Tree #",i, sep = ""))
}

mydf <- do.call(rbind.data.frame, mydf.list)
mydf

mytreeplot <- ggtree(mytrees, aes(color = myLength)) + facet_wrap(~.id, ncol=4)
mytreeplot <- mytreeplot %<+% mydf +
  geom_treescale(offset=1.25) +
  scale_color_continuous(low='darkgreen', high='red', name= 'a rate') +
  ggtitle(paste("My cool trees")) +
  theme(legend.position="right")

mytreeplot #Ok, we get the plot, but as you can see, some branches
# #are not coloured (and I also think, that the branches are not
# #coloured in the correct order)

mytreeplot$data

# #Ugly hack, replacing the tree ".id"
mytreeplot$data[".id"] <- mytreeplot$data["myTreeID"]
mytreeplot$data
mytreeplot #R never stops calculating and we have to abort
# #the calculation
